text:
Lucas Raymond is carrying a Red Wings attack that has had to find offense without Dylan Larkin, whose trade standoff has hung over Detroit's season. After a loss to Boston, the Detroit Free Press put his message in its headline: the Red Wings have to find more offense.

He is doing his part. Raymond has 10 goals and 23 points in 24 games, 11 of those points on the power play, and he ranks 49th of 568 skaters in our wins added. He has scored in five of his last ten games. His shooting is a little hot (15.4% against a likely range around 14%), but his chance creation, about 1.1 expected goals per 60 minutes on his own shots, is well above last season's 0.78, so most of this looks earned.

Evolving-Hockey had him 26th among 401 forwards last season, against competition in the 90th percentile, and he drew more penalties than he took. One thing to watch: his ice time has dipped by about a minute and a half over the last ten games. On a team that lost seven of those ten, that is worth keeping an eye on.
